result.title: JockeyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Horse-Racing Decision-Making
result.summary: Repeated event forecasting requires extracting predictive signals from noisy evidence and evaluating their value across successive decisions. We introduce JockeyBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that studies this problem through historical Japanese horse racing. The protocol combines time-gated evidence, priced tools, paired frozen-program controls, and two workflows: executing an LLM-written predictor or acquiring evidence for a fresh per-race LLM forecast. Evaluation separates forecast quality, benchmark-specific net utility, and retrospective betting returns and risk under fixed decision rules. Across 28 model--scaffold configurations on 324 races, paired tests identify seven revision gains and two declines after multiple-testing correction. Yet every configuration has negative mean profit under capped-Kelly settlement. In a four-model comparison, the reusable-program workflow has higher mean betting profit and lower research fees, although both workflows lose on average. Further diagnostics reveal that mean probability bias reverses on selected bets and that profitable individual runs can depend on concentrated returns. These findings motivate evaluating predictive competence, adaptation, resource use, and decision value separately when assessing agents for repeated event forecasting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 JockeyBench，以历史日本赛马为场景构建 LLM agent 重复事件预测基准，结合时间门控证据、付费工具与冻结程序配对对照，在 324 场比赛、28 种模型配置上分别评估预测质量、净效用与固定规则下的下注收益和风险。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「付费证据获取 + 配对冻结对照 + 区分预测质量与决策价值/成本」的评测协议，可供核查如何归因与计量 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 步骤的增益和代价；但对象为纯文本 agent 决策，未涉及视觉推理或内部推理状态。
